## Probability distributions {.title-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Week 2</div>

<div class="concept-line" style="margin-top:1em;">
The shape of probability.
</div>

## What did probability give us? {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Recall from Week 1</div>

<div class="flow-row">
  <div class="flow-node">Experiment</div>
  <div class="flow-arrow">→</div>
  <div class="flow-node observed">Possible outcomes</div>
  <div class="flow-arrow">→</div>
  <div class="flow-node probability">Events</div>
  <div class="flow-arrow">→</div>
  <div class="flow-node estimate">Numbers</div>
</div>

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
<div class="definition-box large-definition">
$$
A \subseteq \Omega \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \mathbb{P}(A)\in[0,1]
$$
</div>
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
<div class="concept-line">
Probability gives numerical structure to uncertainty.
</div>
:::

::: {.notes}
Use this slide to reconnect students to Week 1 without spending too much time reviewing formal probability spaces.
:::

## Outcomes do not all occur equally often {.motivation-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Two pharmaceutical motivations</div>

<div class="dist-grid-2">
  <div class="dist-card model-border fragment fade-up">
  <div class="dist-title">Tablet press</div>
  <div class="dist-sub">The nominal target is 2.000 g. But every tablet is not exactly 2.000 g.</div>
  <div class="weight-row">
  <img src="figures/tablet.jpg" alt="tablet" class="step-image">
  </div>
  </div>
  <div class="dist-card warning-border fragment fade-up">
  <div class="dist-title">Automatic camera inspection</div>
  <div class="dist-sub">A faulty tablet is expected in 0.1% of presses. How long can the line run without seeing a rejection?</div>
  <div class="dist-eq">$0.999^{1,000}$ &nbsp;vs.&nbsp; $0.999^{1,000,000}$</div>
  <div class="weight-row">
  <img src="figures/machine_vision.jpg" alt="machinevision" class="step-image">
  </div>
  </div>
</div>

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
<div class="concept-line">
A distribution describes how probability is spread across possible outcomes.
</div>
:::

::: {.notes}
These examples foreshadow both continuous and discrete distributions. Tablet mass is continuous. Fault/no fault per press is binary, and the waiting time until first failure is discrete.

Do not calculate yet. Use these as curiosity hooks.
:::

## A distribution is the shape of uncertainty {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">From isolated events to a whole pattern</div>

<div class="dist-grid-2">
  <div class="dist-card fragment fade-up">
  <div class="dist-title">One event</div>
  <div class="dist-sub">A single probability question:</div>
  <div class="dist-eq" style="--eq-size: 2em;">$\mathbb{P}(A)=0.30$</div>
  </div>
  <div class="dist-card fragment fade-up probability-border">
  <div class="dist-title">Many possible outcomes</div>
  <div class="dist-sub">Probability is allocated across the entire outcome space.</div>
  <div class="weight-row">
  <div class="weight-bar" style="height:25%;"><span>1</span></div>
  <div class="weight-bar" style="height:42%;"><span>2</span></div>
  <div class="weight-bar" style="height:76%;"><span>3</span></div>
  <div class="weight-bar" style="height:56%;"><span>4</span></div>
  <div class="weight-bar" style="height:31%;"><span>5</span></div>
  </div>
  </div>
</div>

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
<div class="takeaway">The same probability rules still apply — but now we study the whole shape.</div>
:::

::: {.notes}
This slide introduces the word “shape” intentionally. Students should begin to imagine a distribution as the pattern of probability weights over possible values.
:::

## Two fundamentally different worlds {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Discrete versus continuous</div>

<div class="discrete-continuous">
  <!-- Left Card: Discrete -->
  <div class="dist-card observed-border fragment fade-up">
  <div class="dist-title">Discrete random variable</div>
  <div class="dist-sub">Possible values are separated. Individual values can have positive probability.</div>
    
  <div class="mini-axis">
  <div class="die-bars">
  <span data-x="1"></span><span data-x="2"></span><span data-x="3"></span>
  <span data-x="4"></span><span data-x="5"></span><span data-x="6"></span>
  </div>
  </div>
    
  <div class="dist-eq">Fair die: $X\in\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}$</div>
    
  <!-- Enclosed Image Container -->
  <div class="media-container">
  <img src="figures/dice.jpg" alt="dice" class="step-image">
  </div>
  </div>

  <!-- Right Card: Continuous -->
  <div class="dist-card model-border fragment fade-up">
  <div class="dist-title">Continuous random variable</div>
  <div class="dist-sub">Possible values fill an interval. Probability belongs to ranges, not exact points.</div>
    
  <div class="mini-axis">
  <div class="uniform-fill"></div>
  </div>
    
  <div class="dist-eq">Random number: $X\in[0,1]$</div>
    
  <!-- Enclosed Video Container (Same size as Image Container) -->
  <div class="media-container">
  <video data-autoplay muted loop playsinline>
  <source src="figures/uniform_01_samples.mp4" type="video/mp4">
  </video>
  </div>
  </div>
</div>

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
<div class="concept-line">
Discrete probability lives on values. Continuous probability lives over intervals.
</div>
:::

::: {.notes}
Use a fair die rather than a coin as the flagship discrete-uniform example. Reserve the coin for Bernoulli.

The main conceptual target: for continuous variables, asking for exactly one value is not the same kind of question as for discrete variables.
:::

## Probability mass versus probability density {.math-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">The height means different things</div>

<div class="dist-grid-2">
  <!-- DISCRETE CARD -->
  <div class="dist-card observed-border fragment fade-up">
  <div class="dist-title">Probability mass function (PMF)</div>
  <div class="dist-sub">The bar height is the exact probability of that point.</div>
    
  <div class="definition-box">$p(x) = \mathbb{P}(X=x)$</div>

  <!-- Visual: Fair Die PMF with X=4 Highlighted -->
  <div class="visual-container">
  <div class="pmf-axis">
  <div class="pmf-bar" style="--h: 60%;"><span class="x-val">1</span></div>
  <div class="pmf-bar" style="--h: 60%;"><span class="x-val">2</span></div>
  <div class="pmf-bar" style="--h: 60%;"><span class="x-val">3</span></div>
  <div class="pmf-bar active" style="--h: 60%;">
  <span class="prob-tag">1/6</span>
  <span class="x-val">4</span>
  </div>
  <div class="pmf-bar" style="--h: 60%;"><span class="x-val">5</span></div>
  <div class="pmf-bar" style="--h: 60%;"><span class="x-val">6</span></div>
  </div>
  </div>

  <div class="definition-box probability">$\mathbb{P}(X=4) = 1/6 \approx 0.167$</div>
  </div>

  <!-- CONTINUOUS CARD -->
  <div class="dist-card model-border fragment fade-up">
  <div class="dist-title">Probability density function (PDF)</div>
  <div class="dist-sub">Curve height is density. Area under the curve is probability.</div>

  <div class="definition-box">$\mathbb{P}(a < X < b) = \int_a^b f(x)\,dx$</div>

  <!-- Visual: Uniform PDF [0,1] with Interval [0.4, 0.6] Highlighted -->
  <div class="visual-container">
  <div class="pdf-axis">
  <!-- Subtle background fill across the entire uniform density [0,1] -->
  <div class="pdf-background-fill"></div>
    
  <!-- Density line f(x) = 1 -->
  <div class="pdf-density-line"></div>
    
  <!-- Shaded region for [0.4, 0.6] -->
  <div class="pdf-interval-fill">
  <span class="area-tag">Area = 0.20</span>
  </div>
    
  <!-- Axis Ticks placed inside the container -->
  <div class="axis-ticks">
  <span style="left: 0%;">0</span>
  <span style="left: 40%;" class="tick-active">0.4</span>
  <span style="left: 60%;" class="tick-active">0.6</span>
  <span style="left: 100%;">1</span>
  </div>
  </div>
  </div>

  <div class="definition-box warning">
  $\mathbb{P}(X=0.5) = 0 \quad \text{vs.} \\ \mathbb{P}(0.4 < X < 0.6) = 0.20$
  </div>
  </div>
</div>

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
<div class="concept-line">
For continuous variables, probability requires width — an interval, not a single point.
</div>
:::

::: {.notes}
This is one of the most important conceptual slides of Week 2. Let students sit with the paradox: a possible exact value has probability zero under a continuous distribution.

Use the phrase: “A point has no width, so it has no area.”
:::

## Where can the variable live? {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Support</div>

<div class="dist-grid-3">
  <div class="dist-card fragment fade-up observed-border">
  <div class="dist-title">Fair die</div>
  <div class="dist-sub">Only six possible values.</div>
  <div class="support-line"><span class="support-pill">1</span><span class="support-pill">2</span><span class="support-pill">3</span><span class="support-pill">4</span><span class="support-pill">5</span><span class="support-pill">6</span></div>
  </div>
  <div class="dist-card fragment fade-up model-border">
  <div class="dist-title">Uniform number</div>
  <div class="dist-sub">Any real value between 0 and 1.</div>
  <div class="support-range"><span>0</span><span>$[0,1]$</span><span>1</span></div>
  </div>
  <div class="dist-card fragment fade-up probability-border">
  <div class="dist-title">Waiting time</div>
  <div class="dist-sub">Cannot be negative, but can be arbitrarily long.</div>
  <div class="support-range"><span>0</span><span>$[0,\infty)$</span><span>∞</span></div>
  </div>
</div>

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
<div class="concept-line">
The support of a distribution is the set of values the random variable can take.
</div>
:::

::: {.notes}
Support is useful vocabulary. Tie it to biological and pharmaceutical constraints: concentrations cannot be negative; proportions are between 0 and 1; counts are nonnegative integers.
:::

## Everything must add up to one {.math-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">The same conservation rule in two forms</div>

<div class="sum-integral-row">
  <div class="definition-box fragment fade-up">
  $$
  \sum_x p(x)=1
  $$
  </div>
  <div class="definition-box fragment fade-up">
  $$
  \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x)\,dx=1
  $$
  </div>
</div>

<div class="dist-grid-2" style="margin-top:.6em;">
  <div class="cdf-panel fragment fade-up">
  <svg viewBox="0 0 300 160" aria-label="Discrete probabilities add to one">
  <line x1="25" y1="135" x2="280" y2="135" class="cdf-axis"/>
  <rect x="45" y="70" width="26" height="65" fill="rgba(123,74,181,.7)"/>
  <rect x="82" y="55" width="26" height="80" fill="rgba(123,74,181,.7)"/>
  <rect x="119" y="88" width="26" height="47" fill="rgba(123,74,181,.7)"/>
  <rect x="156" y="42" width="26" height="93" fill="rgba(123,74,181,.7)"/>
  <rect x="193" y="96" width="26" height="39" fill="rgba(123,74,181,.7)"/>
  <rect x="230" y="82" width="26" height="53" fill="rgba(123,74,181,.7)"/>
  </svg>
  <div class="cdf-caption">discrete pieces add</div>
  </div>
  <div class="cdf-panel fragment fade-up">
  <svg viewBox="0 0 300 160" aria-label="Continuous density integrates to one">
  <line x1="25" y1="135" x2="280" y2="135" class="cdf-axis"/>
  <path d="M25,135 C70,135 85,20 150,20 C215,20 230,135 280,135 L25,135 Z" fill="rgba(123,74,181,.20)"/>
  <path d="M25,135 C70,135 85,20 150,20 C215,20 230,135 280,135" class="widget-path"/>
  </svg>
  <div class="cdf-caption">continuous area integrates</div>
  </div>
</div>

::: {.notes}
This slide reinforces a single intuitive conservation law: all probability goes somewhere. In discrete cases, add the pieces; in continuous cases, integrate the area.
:::

## One definition unifies both worlds {.math-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Cumulative distribution function</div>

<div class="definition-box large-definition fragment fade-up">
$$
F(x)=\mathbb{P}(X\leq x)
$$
</div>

<div class="dist-grid-2" style="margin-top:.55em;">
  <div class="cdf-panel fragment fade-up">
  <svg viewBox="0 0 300 160" aria-label="Step CDF">
  <line x1="25" y1="135" x2="280" y2="135" class="cdf-axis"/><line x1="25" y1="135" x2="25" y2="20" class="cdf-axis"/>
  <path d="M25,135 L62,135 L62,116 L99,116 L99,97 L136,97 L136,78 L173,78 L173,59 L210,59 L210,40 L247,40 L247,21 L280,21" class="cdf-step"/>
  </svg>
  <div class="cdf-caption">discrete CDF jumps</div>
  </div>
  <div class="cdf-panel fragment fade-up">
  <svg viewBox="0 0 300 160" aria-label="Smooth CDF">
  <line x1="25" y1="135" x2="280" y2="135" class="cdf-axis"/><line x1="25" y1="135" x2="25" y2="20" class="cdf-axis"/>
  <path d="M25,132 C70,130 88,116 108,93 C130,68 143,50 165,39 C190,28 225,25 280,23" class="cdf-curve"/>
  </svg>
  <div class="cdf-caption">continuous CDF flows</div>
  </div>
</div>

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
<div class="concept-line">
The CDF always answers the same question: how much probability has accumulated up to this point?
</div>
:::

::: {.notes}
Stress that the CDF is often easier to use for “at most” or “less than” questions. It will become crucial for p-values, quantiles and confidence intervals later.
:::

## Watch probability accumulate {.exercise-slide}

<script>
(function () {

  function initCDFWidget() {
    const input = document.getElementById("cdfX");
    const valueDisplay = document.getElementById("cdfValue");
    const svg = document.getElementById("cdfSvg");
    if (!input || !valueDisplay || !svg) return;
    // Prevent duplicate listeners if Reveal re-enters/reinitializes.
    if (svg.dataset.initialized === "true") {
      render();
      return;
    }
    svg.dataset.initialized = "true";
    function pdf(x) {
      return Math.exp(-0.5 * x * x) / Math.sqrt(2 * Math.PI);
    }
    // Abramowitz-Stegun approximation to standard Normal CDF
    function cdf(x) {
      const z = Math.abs(x);
      const t = 1 / (1 + 0.2316419 * z);
      const d = 0.3989422804014327 * Math.exp(-0.5 * z * z);
      const tail =
        d * t *
        (
          0.319381530 +
          t * (
            -0.356563782 +
            t * (
              1.781477937 +
              t * (
                -1.821255978 +
                t * 1.330274429
              )
            )
          )
        );
      return x >= 0 ? 1 - tail : tail;
    }
    // ------------------------------------------------------------
    // Coordinate mappings
    // ------------------------------------------------------------
    const xMin = -3.5;
    const xMax =  3.5;
    const plotLeft  = 60;
    const plotRight = 660;
    const plotWidth = plotRight - plotLeft;
    const mapX = x =>
      plotLeft + ((x - xMin) / (xMax - xMin)) * plotWidth;
    // PDF panel
    const pdfTop = 35;
    const pdfBottom = 175;
    const mapYPdf = y =>
      pdfBottom - (y / 0.42) * (pdfBottom - pdfTop);
    // CDF panel
    const cdfTop = 235;
    const cdfBottom = 390;
    const mapYCdf = y =>
      cdfBottom - y * (cdfBottom - cdfTop);
    function samplePath(fn, from, to, mapY, step = 0.035) {
      const pts = [];
      for (let x = from; x <= to + 1e-9; x += step) {
        pts.push([
          mapX(x),
          mapY(fn(x))
        ]);
      }
      // Make sure exact endpoint is included.
      if (pts.length === 0 || from < to) {
        pts.push([
          mapX(to),
          mapY(fn(to))
        ]);
      }
      return pts;
    }
    function pathFromPoints(points) {
      if (!points.length) return "";
      return points
        .map((p, i) =>
          `${i === 0 ? "M" : "L"} ${p[0].toFixed(2)} ${p[1].toFixed(2)}`
        )
        .join(" ");
    }
    function render() {
      const currentX = Number(input.value);
      const currentCDF = cdf(currentX);
      valueDisplay.textContent = currentCDF.toFixed(3);
      // ----------------------------------------------------------
      // PDF paths
      // ----------------------------------------------------------
      const pdfPoints = samplePath(
        pdf,
        xMin,
        xMax,
        mapYPdf
      );
      const shadedPdfPoints = samplePath(
        pdf,
        xMin,
        currentX,
        mapYPdf
      );
      let areaPath =
        `M ${mapX(xMin)} ${pdfBottom} ` +
        shadedPdfPoints
          .map(p => `L ${p[0].toFixed(2)} ${p[1].toFixed(2)}`)
          .join(" ") +
        ` L ${mapX(currentX)} ${pdfBottom} Z`;
      // ----------------------------------------------------------
      // CDF paths
      // ----------------------------------------------------------
      const fullCdfPoints = samplePath(
        cdf,
        xMin,
        xMax,
        mapYCdf
      );
      const activeCdfPoints = samplePath(
        cdf,
        xMin,
        currentX,
        mapYCdf
      );
      const currentPX = mapX(currentX);
      const currentPY = mapYCdf(currentCDF);
      svg.innerHTML = `
        <!-- ==================== PDF ==================== -->
        <text x="60" y="25" class="panel-label">
          PDF: density f(x); shaded area = F(x)
        </text>
        <path
          d="${areaPath}"
          class="widget-area">
        </path>
        <path
          d="${pathFromPoints(pdfPoints)}"
          class="widget-path">
        </path>
        <line
          x1="${plotLeft}" y1="${pdfBottom}"
          x2="${plotRight}" y2="${pdfBottom}"
          class="widget-axis">
        </line>
        <line
          x1="${currentPX}" y1="${pdfTop}"
          x2="${currentPX}" y2="${pdfBottom}"
          class="widget-line">
        </line>
        <text
          x="${currentPX}"
          y="${pdfBottom + 18}"
          class="widget-label active"
          text-anchor="middle">
          ${currentX.toFixed(2)}
        </text>
        <!-- Divider -->
        <line
          x1="45" y1="205"
          x2="675" y2="205"
          class="panel-divider">
        </line>
        <!-- ==================== CDF ==================== -->
        <text x="60" y="226" class="panel-label">
          CDF: F(x) = P(X ≤ x)
        </text>
        <path
          d="${pathFromPoints(fullCdfPoints)}"
          class="widget-path-faint">
        </path>
        <path
          d="${pathFromPoints(activeCdfPoints)}"
          class="widget-path-blue">
        </path>
        <line
          x1="${plotLeft}" y1="${cdfBottom}"
          x2="${plotRight}" y2="${cdfBottom}"
          class="widget-axis">
        </line>
        <line
          x1="${plotLeft}" y1="${currentPY}"
          x2="${currentPX}" y2="${currentPY}"
          class="widget-line-horizontal">
        </line>
        <line
          x1="${currentPX}" y1="${cdfBottom}"
          x2="${currentPX}" y2="${currentPY}"
          class="widget-line">
        </line>
        <circle
          cx="${currentPX}"
          cy="${currentPY}"
          r="6"
          class="cdf-tracker-point">
        </circle>
        <!-- X axis labels -->
        <text x="${mapX(-3)}" y="413"
          class="widget-label"
          text-anchor="middle">−3</text>
        <text x="${mapX(0)}" y="413"
          class="widget-label"
          text-anchor="middle">0</text>
        <text x="${mapX(3)}" y="413"
          class="widget-label"
          text-anchor="middle">3</text>
        <!-- Y axis labels -->
        <text x="50" y="${mapYCdf(0) + 4}"
          class="widget-label"
          text-anchor="end">0</text>
        <text x="50" y="${mapYCdf(0.5) + 4}"
          class="widget-label"
          text-anchor="end">0.5</text>
        <text x="50" y="${mapYCdf(1) + 4}"
          class="widget-label"
          text-anchor="end">1</text>
      `;
    }
    input.addEventListener("input", render);
    // Initial drawing
    render();
  }

  // The markup above this script already exists, so initialize now.
  initCDFWidget();

  // Fallback if Quarto/Reveal timing differs.
  window.addEventListener("load", initCDFWidget);

  // RevealJS fallback when revisiting the slide.
  if (window.Reveal) {
    Reveal.on("ready", initCDFWidget);
    Reveal.on("slidechanged", initCDFWidget);
  }

})();
</script>

<div class="try-label">Interactive concept slide</div>

<div class="ojs-note">Move the cutoff. Probability to the left becomes the CDF value.</div>

<div class="cdf-widget" id="cdfWidget">
  <div class="week02-control-row">
  <label class="week02-control">Cutoff x
  <input id="cdfX" type="range" min="-3" max="3" value="0" step="0.05">
  </label>
  <div class="week02-control">Distribution
  <div><strong class="model">Standard Normal</strong></div>
  </div>
  <div class="week02-control">CDF value F(x)
  <div><strong id="cdfValue" class="probability">0.500</strong></div>
  </div>
  </div>

  <svg id="cdfSvg"
       class="week02-svg dual-panel"
       viewBox="0 0 700 430"
       aria-label="Interactive Normal PDF and CDF">
  </svg>
</div>

::: {.notes}
This widget is intentionally simple: a standard normal curve, a vertical cutoff, and the shaded probability to the left. It visually links the PDF to the CDF.
:::

## What probability are you asking for? {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">The wording determines the area</div>

<div class="question-types">
  <div class="qtype-card fragment fade-up">
  <div class="qtype-title">Exactly</div>
  <div class="qtype-eq">$\mathbb{P}(X=x)$</div>
  <div class="qtype-note">meaningful for discrete values</div>
  </div>
  <div class="qtype-card fragment fade-up">
  <div class="qtype-title">At most</div>
  <div class="qtype-eq">$\mathbb{P}(X\leq x)$</div>
  <div class="qtype-note">lower cumulative probability</div>
  </div>
  <div class="qtype-card fragment fade-up">
  <div class="qtype-title">At least</div>
  <div class="qtype-eq">$\mathbb{P}(X\geq x)$</div>
  <div class="qtype-note">upper tail probability</div>
  </div>
  <div class="qtype-card fragment fade-up">
  <div class="qtype-title">Between</div>
  <div class="qtype-eq">$\mathbb{P}(a<X<b)$</div>
  <div class="qtype-note">interval probability</div>
  </div>
</div>

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
<div class="concept-line">
“Exactly”, “at most”, “at least” and “between” are different probability questions.
</div>
:::

::: {.notes}
This slide prepares the tablet mass widget. Emphasize how often students answer the wrong probability question because the wording is imprecise.
:::

## Tablet press laboratory {.exercise-slide}

<div class="try-label">Interactive slide for students at home</div>

<div class="tablet-widget" id="tabletWidget">
  <div class="week02-control-row">
  <label class="week02-control">
  Question
  <select id="tabletMode">
  <option value="between">lower ≤ X ≤ upper</option>
  <option value="below">X ≤ cutoff</option>
  <option value="above">X ≥ cutoff</option>
  </select>
  </label>
  <label class="week02-control" id="tabletLowerControl">
  <span id="tabletLowerLabel">Lower bound, g</span>
  <input
  id="tabletLower"
  type="range"
  min="1.96"
  max="2.04"
  value="1.99"
  step="0.001">
  </label>
  <label class="week02-control" id="tabletUpperControl">
  <span id="tabletUpperLabel">Upper bound, g</span>
  <input
  id="tabletUpper"
  type="range"
  min="1.96"
  max="2.04"
  value="2.01"
  step="0.001">
  </label>
  </div>
  <svg
  id="tabletSvg"
  class="week02-svg"
  viewBox="0 0 700 260"
  aria-label="Tablet mass normal probability explorer">
  </svg>
  <div class="week02-output">
  <div class="out">
  <span>model</span>
  <strong>$X\sim \mathcal{N}(2.000,0.008^2)$</strong>
  </div>
  <div class="out">
  <span>region</span>
  <strong id="tabletBounds">1.990–2.010 g</strong>
  </div>
  <div class="out">
  <span>probability</span>
  <strong id="tabletProb" class="probability">0.789</strong>
  </div>
  </div>
</div>

<script>
(function () {

  const widget = document.getElementById("tabletWidget");
  if (!widget) return;

  const modeInput = document.getElementById("tabletMode");
  const lowerInput = document.getElementById("tabletLower");
  const upperInput = document.getElementById("tabletUpper");

  const lowerControl = document.getElementById("tabletLowerControl");
  const upperControl = document.getElementById("tabletUpperControl");

  const lowerLabel = document.getElementById("tabletLowerLabel");
  const upperLabel = document.getElementById("tabletUpperLabel");

  const boundsDisplay = document.getElementById("tabletBounds");
  const probDisplay = document.getElementById("tabletProb");
  const svg = document.getElementById("tabletSvg");

  if (!modeInput || !lowerInput || !upperInput || !svg) return;

  const mu = 2.000;
  const sigma = 0.008;

  // Plot range extends beyond slider bounds so tails remain visible.
  const xMin = 1.96;
  const xMax = 2.04;

  const left = 45;
  const right = 665;

  const baseline = 225;
  const top = 20;

  // ------------------------------------------------------------
  // Normal PDF / CDF
  // ------------------------------------------------------------

  function pdf(x) {
    const z = (x - mu) / sigma;
    return (
      Math.exp(-0.5 * z * z) /
      (sigma * Math.sqrt(2 * Math.PI))
    );
  }
  function standardNormalCDF(z) {
    const a = Math.abs(z);
    const t = 1 / (1 + 0.2316419 * a);
    const d =
      0.3989422804014327 *
      Math.exp(-0.5 * a * a);
    const tail =
      d * t *
      (
        0.319381530 +
        t * (
          -0.356563782 +
          t * (
            1.781477937 +
            t * (
              -1.821255978 +
              t * 1.330274429
            )
          )
        )
      );
    return z >= 0 ? 1 - tail : tail;
  }

  function cdf(x) {
    return standardNormalCDF((x - mu) / sigma);
  }

  // ------------------------------------------------------------
  // Coordinate mapping
  // ------------------------------------------------------------

  function mapX(x) {
    return left + ((x - xMin) / (xMax - xMin)) * (right - left);
  }

  // Maximum Normal density occurs at mu
  const pdfMax = pdf(mu);

  function mapY(y) {
    return baseline - (y / pdfMax) * (baseline - top);
  }

  // ------------------------------------------------------------
  // Curve construction
  // ------------------------------------------------------------

  function curvePoints(from, to, step = 0.0002) {
    const pts = [];
    if (to < from) return pts;
    for (let x = from; x < to; x += step) {
      pts.push([mapX(x), mapY(pdf(x))]);
    }
    // Exact endpoint
    pts.push([mapX(to), mapY(pdf(to))]);
    return pts;
  }

  function pointsToLines(points) {
    return points
      .map(([x, y]) => `L ${x.toFixed(2)} ${y.toFixed(2)}`)
      .join(" ");
  }

  // ------------------------------------------------------------
  // Correct probability-area polygons
  // ------------------------------------------------------------

  function areaBetween(lower, upper) {
    const pts = curvePoints(lower, upper);
    return [
      // Start ON THE BASELINE under lower bound
      `M ${mapX(lower)} ${baseline}`,
      // Rise vertically to curve
      `L ${mapX(lower)} ${mapY(pdf(lower))}`,
      // Follow curve from lower -> upper
      pointsToLines(pts.slice(1)),
      // Drop vertically to baseline
      `L ${mapX(upper)} ${baseline}`,
      // Close along baseline
      "Z"
    ].join(" ");
  }

  function areaBelow(cutoff) {
    const pts = curvePoints(xMin, cutoff);
    return [
      // Start on baseline at left edge
      `M ${mapX(xMin)} ${baseline}`,
      // Rise to curve
      `L ${mapX(xMin)} ${mapY(pdf(xMin))}`,
      // Follow curve left -> cutoff
      pointsToLines(pts.slice(1)),
      // Drop vertically at cutoff
      `L ${mapX(cutoff)} ${baseline}`,
      // Close along baseline
      "Z"
    ].join(" ");
  }

  function areaAbove(cutoff) {
    const pts = curvePoints(cutoff, xMax);
    return [
      // Start on baseline directly under cutoff
      `M ${mapX(cutoff)} ${baseline}`,
      // Rise vertically to curve at cutoff
      `L ${mapX(cutoff)} ${mapY(pdf(cutoff))}`,
      // Follow curve cutoff -> right edge
      pointsToLines(pts.slice(1)),
      // Drop vertically at right edge
      `L ${mapX(xMax)} ${baseline}`,
      // Close along baseline
      "Z"
    ].join(" ");
  }

  // ------------------------------------------------------------
  // Full density curve
  // ------------------------------------------------------------

  function fullCurvePath() {
    const pts = curvePoints(xMin, xMax);
    if (!pts.length) return "";
    const [firstX, firstY] = pts[0];
    return (
      `M ${firstX.toFixed(2)} ${firstY.toFixed(2)} ` +
      pointsToLines(pts.slice(1))
    );
  }

  // ------------------------------------------------------------
  // Rendering
  // ------------------------------------------------------------

  function render() {
    let lower = Number(lowerInput.value);
    let upper = Number(upperInput.value);
    const mode = modeInput.value;
    if (mode === "between") {
      lowerInput.disabled = false;
      upperInput.disabled = false;
      lowerLabel.textContent = "Lower bound, g";
      upperLabel.textContent = "Upper bound, g";
    } else if (mode === "below") {
      lowerInput.disabled = false;
      upperInput.disabled = true;
      lowerLabel.textContent = "Cutoff, g";
      upperLabel.textContent = "Not used";
    } else if (mode === "above") {
      lowerInput.disabled = true;
      upperInput.disabled = false;
      lowerLabel.textContent = "Not used";
      upperLabel.textContent = "Cutoff, g";
    }
    // Prevent inverted interval.
    if (lower > upper) {
      if (document.activeElement === lowerInput) {
        upper = lower;
        upperInput.value = upper;
      } else {
        lower = upper;
        lowerInput.value = lower;
      }
    }
    let probability;
    let areaPath;
    let boundsText;
    if (mode === "between") {
      probability =
        cdf(upper) - cdf(lower);
      areaPath =
        areaBetween(lower, upper);
      boundsText =
        `${lower.toFixed(3)}–${upper.toFixed(3)} g`;
    } else if (mode === "below") {
      probability =
        cdf(lower);
      areaPath =
        areaBelow(lower);
      boundsText =
        `X ≤ ${lower.toFixed(3)} g`;
    } else {
      probability =
        1 - cdf(upper);
      areaPath =
        areaAbove(upper);
      boundsText =
        `X ≥ ${upper.toFixed(3)} g`;
    }
    boundsDisplay.textContent = boundsText;
    probDisplay.textContent = probability.toFixed(3);
    // ----------------------------------------------------------
    // Boundary lines
    // ----------------------------------------------------------
    let boundaryLines = "";
    if (mode === "between") {
      boundaryLines = `
        <line
          x1="${mapX(lower)}"
          y1="${mapY(pdf(lower))}"
          x2="${mapX(lower)}"
          y2="${baseline}"
          class="widget-line">
        </line>
        <line
          x1="${mapX(upper)}"
          y1="${mapY(pdf(upper))}"
          x2="${mapX(upper)}"
          y2="${baseline}"
          class="widget-line">
        </line>
      `;
    } else if (mode === "below") {
      boundaryLines = `
        <line
          x1="${mapX(lower)}"
          y1="${mapY(pdf(lower))}"
          x2="${mapX(lower)}"
          y2="${baseline}"
          class="widget-line">
        </line>
      `;
    } else {
      boundaryLines = `
        <line
          x1="${mapX(upper)}"
          y1="${mapY(pdf(upper))}"
          x2="${mapX(upper)}"
          y2="${baseline}"
          class="widget-line">
        </line>
      `;
    }
    svg.innerHTML = `
      <!-- probability area -->
      <path
        d="${areaPath}"
        class="widget-area">
      </path>
      <!-- complete normal density -->
      <path
        d="${fullCurvePath()}"
        class="widget-path">
      </path>
      <!-- x-axis -->
      <line
        x1="${left}"
        y1="${baseline}"
        x2="${right}"
        y2="${baseline}"
        class="widget-axis">
      </line>
      ${boundaryLines}
      <!-- mean -->
      <line
        x1="${mapX(mu)}"
        y1="${mapY(pdf(mu))}"
        x2="${mapX(mu)}"
        y2="${baseline}"
        class="tablet-mean-line">
      </line>
      <text
        x="${mapX(mu)}"
        y="${baseline + 21}"
        class="widget-label"
        text-anchor="middle">
        2.000
      </text>
      <text
        x="${mapX(1.96)}"
        y="${baseline + 21}"
        class="widget-label"
        text-anchor="middle">
        1.96
      </text>
      <text
        x="${mapX(2.04)}"
        y="${baseline + 21}"
        class="widget-label"
        text-anchor="middle">
        2.04
      </text>
    `;
  }

  // ------------------------------------------------------------
  // Controls
  // ------------------------------------------------------------

  modeInput.addEventListener("change", render);
  lowerInput.addEventListener("input", render);
  upperInput.addEventListener("input", render);

  render();

})();
</script>

::: {.notes}
Use this as the central interactive slide for Week 2. The key message is not numerical precision; it is that the probability question determines which area under the curve is relevant.

Suggested live sequence: ask for between 1.99 and 2.01, then switch to at least 1.99. Same bound, completely different probability question.
:::

## Meet the normal distribution {.math-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">After the intuition, the notation</div>

<div class="dist-grid-2">
  <div class="dist-card model-border fragment fade-up">
  <div class="dist-title">Notation</div>
  <div class="definition-box large-definition">$X\sim \mathcal{N}(\mu,\sigma^2)$</div>
  <div class="dist-sub">Two parameters uniquely define the model: location and spread.</div>
  </div>
  <div class="dist-card fragment fade-up">
  <div class="dist-title">Density</div>
  <div class="definition-box" style="font-size:.62em;">
  $$f(x)=\frac{1}{\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}}\,e^{-\frac12\left(\frac{x-\mu}{\sigma}\right)^2}$$
  </div>
  <div class="dist-sub">Recognize the formula. Do not memorize it.</div>
  </div>
</div>

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
<div class="concept-line">
For the Gaussian model, $\mu$ moves the center and $\sigma$ controls the spread.
</div>

<div class="concept-line">
Why Gaussian normal distribution is so common in nature: it models an outcome that is the sum of many tiny independent contributions.
</div>
:::

::: {.notes}
Tell students that formula recognition is enough here. They should understand what the parameters do and how to interpret probability regions.
:::

<div class="eyebrow">Percentiles and inverse CDF thinking</div>

<div class="normal-mini fragment fade-up">

## Mean: where is the distribution centered? {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Expected value as a balance point</div>

<div class="definition-box fragment fade-up">
$$
E[X] = \sum_x x\,p(x) \quad\text{or}\quad E[X]=\int x f(x)\,dx
$$
</div>

<style>
/* 1. Animate the main beam to balance/teeter around its center */
@keyframes beamTeeter {
  0%   { transform: rotate(0deg) translateY(0px); }
  25%  { transform: rotate(-1.8deg) translateY(-2px); }
  50%  { transform: rotate(0.8deg) translateY(1px); }
  75%  { transform: rotate(-0.8deg) translateY(-1px); }
  100% { transform: rotate(0deg) translateY(0px); }
}

/* 2. Optional gentle bounce for the dots to feel organic */
@keyframes dotJiggle {
  0%, 100% { transform: translateY(0); }
  50%      { transform: translateY(-1.5px); }
}

/* Apply animations to classes */
.moment-beam {
  position: relative;
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  /* Ensure the rotation pivot point is centered around the beam/fulcrum */
  transform-origin: 50% 50%;
  animation: beamTeeter 4.5s ease-in-out infinite;
}

/* Mass dots styling + subtle float */
.mass-dot {
  position: absolute;
  width: 12px;
  height: 12px;
  background-color: #2563eb; /* Blue points */
  border-radius: 50%;
  animation: dotJiggle 2.5s ease-in-out infinite alternate;
}

/* Fulcrum (Green Triangle/Point) */
.balance-point {
  /* ... your existing styling ... */
  border-bottom-color: #16a34a; /* Green fulcrum */
}
</style>

<!-- Your existing HTML structure -->
<div class="moment-beam fragment fade-up">
  <div class="beam-line"></div>
  <span class="mass-dot" style="left:18%; animation-delay: 0.1s;"></span>
  <span class="mass-dot" style="left:29%; animation-delay: 0.3s;"></span>
  <span class="mass-dot" style="left:36%; animation-delay: 0.2s;"></span>
  <span class="mass-dot" style="left:48%; animation-delay: 0.5s;"></span>
  <span class="mass-dot" style="left:58%; animation-delay: 0.4s;"></span>
  <span class="mass-dot" style="left:66%; animation-delay: 0.2s;"></span>
  <span class="mass-dot" style="left:75%; animation-delay: 0.6s;"></span>
  <div class="balance-point"></div>
  <div class="balance-label">$E[X]$</div>
</div>

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
<div class="concept-line">
The expected value (mean, also called **first moment**) is the balancing point of the probability distribution.
</div>
:::

::: {.notes}
Use this as a physical metaphor, then remind students that the mean can be pulled by long tails. That sets up skewness.
:::

## Variance: how far do values wander? {.math-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Second central moment</div>

<div class="definition-box fragment fade-up">
$$
\operatorname{Var}(X)=E[(X-\mu)^2], \qquad SD(X)=\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(X)}
$$
</div>

<style>
@keyframes arrowStretch {
  0%, 100% { transform: scaleX(1); }
  50%      { transform: scaleX(1.25); }
}

.dev.animated {
  transform-origin: 50% 50%;
  animation: arrowStretch 3s ease-in-out infinite;
}
</style>

<div class="variance-lines fragment fade-up">
  <div class="axis"></div>
  <div class="mu-line"></div>
  <span class="v-dot" style="left:18%;"></span>
  <span class="v-dot" style="left:35%;"></span>
  <span class="v-dot" style="left:57%;"></span>
  <span class="v-dot" style="left:78%;"></span>
  <!-- Added "animated" class -->
  <span class="dev longest animated" style="left:18%; width:60%;"></span>
</div>

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
<div class="concept-line">
Variance (also called **second central moment**) measures spread around the mean using squared deviations.
</div>
:::

::: {.notes}
Students should know variance is in squared units and standard deviation returns to original units. Use tablet mass: variance in g² is less intuitive than SD in g.
:::

State the mean/median/mode order as a visual heuristic, not a theorem for every possible distribution.

:::

## Why tails matter {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Kurtosis as extreme-event propensity</div>

<div class="tail-compare">
  <div class="normal-mini fragment fade-up">
  <svg
    id="tailCompareSvg"
    class="empirical-rule-svg"
    viewBox="0 0 700 220"
    preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"
    aria-label="Normal versus heavy tail">
  </svg>
  </div>
  <div class="tail-legend">
  <div class="tail-legend-item fragment fade-up"><strong>Same center</strong>, very different probability of distant values.</div>
  <div class="tail-legend-item fragment fade-up"><strong>Kurtosis</strong> is best remembered here as tail/extreme-value behavior.</div>
  <div class="tail-legend-item fragment fade-up"><strong>Outliers</strong> may be surprising under one model and ordinary under another.</div>
  </div>
</div>

::: {.notes}
Avoid the common oversimplification “kurtosis equals peakedness.” For this course, emphasize heavy tails and extreme values.
:::

The Gaussian is friendly. The Cauchy reminds us that not all distributions have familiar summaries.

:::

::: {.notes}
This slide uses a CSS/SVG animation as the default. It is also an excellent candidate for a future Manim animation because the continuous motion carries mathematical meaning.

The rigorous idea: if an angle is uniform and the intersection coordinate is tan(theta), the resulting distribution is Cauchy-like.
:::

This replaces an encyclopedia of formulas with a map. Students should first learn which real-world mechanism each distribution represents.

## Discrete: one trial to many trials {.math-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Binary and finite equal-chance mechanisms</div>

<div class="dist-grid-4">
  <div class="dist-card observed-border fragment fade-up">
  <div class="dist-title">Degenerate</div>
  <div class="dist-sub">The outcome is fixed.</div>
  <div class="dist-eq">$\mathbb{P}(X=c)=1$</div>
  <svg id="degeneratePmf" class="mini-pmf" viewBox="0 0 240 135"></svg>
  </div>
  <div class="dist-card observed-border fragment fade-up">
  <div class="dist-title">Discrete uniform</div>
  <div class="dist-sub">Finite outcomes equally likely.</div>
  <div class="dist-eq">$\mathbb{P}(X=x)=1/k$</div>
  <label class="mini-control">k = <strong id="uniformKValue">6</strong>
  <input id="uniformK" type="range" min="1" max="10" value="6" step="1">
  </label>
  <svg id="uniformPmf" class="mini-pmf" viewBox="0 0 240 135"></svg>
  </div>
  <div class="dist-card probability-border fragment fade-up">
  <div class="dist-title">Bernoulli</div>
  <div class="dist-sub">One yes/no experiment.</div>
  <div class="dist-eq">$\mathbb{P}(X=1)=p$</div>
  <label class="mini-control">p = <strong id="bernoulliPValue">0.50</strong>
  <input id="bernoulliP" type="range" min="0" max="1" value="0.5" step="0.05">
  </label>
  <svg id="bernoulliPmf" class="mini-pmf" viewBox="0 0 240 135"></svg>
  </div>
  <div class="dist-card probability-border fragment fade-up">
  <div class="dist-title">Binomial</div>
  <div class="dist-sub">Successes in $n$ independent Bernoulli trials.</div>
  <div class="dist-eq">$\mathbb{P}(X=k)=\binom nkp^k(1-p)^{n-k}$</div>
  <div class="mini-control-row">
  <label class="mini-control">n = <strong id="binomialNValue">6</strong>
  <input id="binomialN" type="range" min="1" max="10" value="6" step="1">
  </label>
  <label class="mini-control">p = <strong id="binomialPValue">0.50</strong>
  <input id="binomialP" type="range" min="0" max="1" value="0.5" step="0.05">
  </label>
  </div>
  <svg id="binomialPmf" class="mini-pmf" viewBox="0 0 240 135"></svg>
  </div>
</div>

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
<div class="takeaway">Coin toss: Bernoulli. Fair die: discrete uniform. Repeated responses: binomial.</div>
:::

::: {.notes}
Do not spend time deriving each formula. The story/mechanism is the learning target. The binomial formula will be used in exercises.
:::

## Discrete: counting and sampling {.math-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Different sampling mechanisms create different distributions</div>

<div class="dist-grid-3">
  <div class="dist-card probability-border fragment fade-up">
  <div class="dist-title">Geometric</div>
  <div class="dist-sub">Trials until the first success.</div>
  <div class="dist-eq">$\mathbb{P}(T=t)=(1-p)^{t-1}p$</div>
  <label class="mini-control">
  p = <strong id="geometricPValue">0.30</strong>
  <input id="geometricP" type="range" min="0.05" max="0.95" value="0.30" step="0.05">
  </label>
  <svg id="geometricPmf" class="mini-pmf" viewBox="0 0 240 135"></svg>
  </div>
  <div class="dist-card observed-border fragment fade-up">
  <div class="dist-title">Hypergeometric</div>
  <div class="dist-sub">Sampling from a finite batch without replacement.</div>
  <div class="dist-eq">$\mathbb{P}(X=k)=\frac{\binom Kk\binom{N-K}{n-k}}{\binom Nn}$</div>
  <div class="mini-control-row-3">
  <label class="mini-control">
  N = <strong id="hyperNValue">20</strong>
  <input id="hyperN" type="range" min="5" max="30" value="20" step="1">
  </label>
  <label class="mini-control">
  K = <strong id="hyperKValue">8</strong>
  <input id="hyperK" type="range" min="1" max="19" value="8" step="1">
  </label>
  <label class="mini-control">
  n = <strong id="hyperSampleValue">5</strong>
  <input id="hyperSample" type="range" min="1" max="20" value="5" step="1">
  </label>
  </div>
  <svg id="hypergeometricPmf" class="mini-pmf" viewBox="0 0 240 135"></svg>
  </div>
  <div class="dist-card model-border fragment fade-up">
  <div class="dist-title">Poisson</div>
  <div class="dist-sub">Count events in a fixed exposure interval.</div>
  <div class="dist-eq">$\mathbb{P}(X=k)=e^{-\lambda}\frac{\lambda^k}{k!}$</div>
  <label class="mini-control">
  λ = <strong id="poissonLambdaValue">3.0</strong>
  <input id="poissonLambda" type="range" min="0.5" max="8" value="3" step="0.5">
  </label>
  <svg id="poissonPmf" class="mini-pmf" viewBox="0 0 240 135"></svg>
  </div>
</div>

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
<div class="concept-line">
Before calculating, identify the experiment that generated the count.
</div>
:::

::: {.notes}
Use the tablet press example for geometric, batch sampling for hypergeometric, and dispensing errors or adverse events per exposure interval for Poisson.
:::

<div class="dist-grid-4">

Keep the Dirac delta simple: a mathematical idealization of all mass at one point. Do not teach generalized functions.

<div class="eyebrow">Additive, multiplicative and heavy-tail behavior</div>

<div class="dist-grid-4">
  <div class="dist-card model-border fragment fade-up">
  <div class="dist-title">Gaussian</div>
  <div class="dist-sub">Additive variation around a center.</div>
  <div class="dist-eq">$\mathcal{N}(\mu,\sigma^2)$</div>
  <div class="mini-control-row">
  <label class="mini-control">
  μ = <strong id="gaussianMuValue">0.0</strong>
  <input id="gaussianMu" type="range" min="-2" max="2" value="0" step="0.25">
  </label>
  <label class="mini-control">
  σ = <strong id="gaussianSigmaValue">1.0</strong>
  <input id="gaussianSigma" type="range" min="0.5" max="2" value="1" step="0.25">
  </label>
  </div>
  <svg id="gaussianDensity" class="mini-density" viewBox="0 0 240 135"></svg>
  </div>
  <div class="dist-card estimate-border fragment fade-up">
  <div class="dist-title">Log-normal</div>
  <div class="dist-sub">Positive values with multiplicative variability.</div>
  <div class="dist-eq">$\log X\sim\mathcal{N}(\mu_{\log},\sigma_{\log}^2)$</div>
  <div class="mini-control-row">
  <label class="mini-control">
  μ<sub>log</sub> = <strong id="lognormalMuValue">0.00</strong>
  <input id="lognormalMu" type="range" min="-1" max="1" value="0" step="0.1">
  </label>
  <label class="mini-control">
  σ<sub>log</sub> = <strong id="lognormalSigmaValue">0.60</strong>
  <input id="lognormalSigma" type="range" min="0.25" max="1.2" value="0.6" step="0.05">
  </label>
  </div>
  <svg id="lognormalDensity" class="mini-density" viewBox="0 0 240 135"></svg>
  </div>
  <div class="dist-card warning-border fragment fade-up">
  <div class="dist-title">Pareto</div>
  <div class="dist-sub">Scaling behavior; few very large values.</div>
  <div class="dist-eq">heavy right tail</div>
  <label class="mini-control">
  α = <strong id="paretoAlphaValue">2.0</strong>
  <input id="paretoAlpha" type="range" min="0.75" max="4" value="2" step="0.25">
  </label>
  <svg id="paretoDensity" class="mini-density" viewBox="0 0 240 135"></svg>
  </div>
  <div class="dist-card warning-border fragment fade-up">
  <div class="dist-title">Cauchy</div>
  <div class="dist-sub">Very heavy symmetric tails; mean/variance undefined.</div>
  <div class="dist-eq">$\operatorname{Cauchy}(x_0,\gamma)$</div>
  <div class="mini-control-row">
  <label class="mini-control">
  x₀ = <strong id="cauchyX0Value">0.0</strong>
  <input id="cauchyX0" type="range" min="-2" max="2" value="0" step="0.25">
  </label>
  <label class="mini-control">
  γ = <strong id="cauchyGammaValue">1.0</strong>
  <input id="cauchyGamma" type="range" min="0.5" max="2" value="1" step="0.25">
  </label>
  </div>
  <svg id="cauchyDensity" class="mini-density" viewBox="0 0 240 135"></svg>
  </div>
</div>

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
<div class="takeaway">Real scientific data often choose the distribution for us: counts, proportions, positive times, concentrations, extremes.</div>
:::

::: {.notes}
Pharmaceutical examples: concentration and clearance often right-skew; assay errors may be approximately Gaussian after calibration; adverse event counts may use Poisson-like models; extreme values require caution.
:::

## Which distribution describes the experiment? {.checkpoint-slide}

<div class="try-label">Checkpoint before calculation</div>

<div class="matching-grid">
  <div class="scenario-list">
  <div class="scenario-item fragment fade-up">A. 20 patients each respond or do not respond.</div>
  <div class="scenario-item fragment fade-up">B. Count dispensing errors during an 8-hour shift.</div>
  <div class="scenario-item fragment fade-up">C. Inspect 5 tablets from a finite batch containing 3 known defects.</div>
  <div class="scenario-item fragment fade-up">D. Count presses until the first camera rejection.</div>
  <div class="scenario-item fragment fade-up">E. Measure time until the first degradation event.</div>
  </div>
  <div class="scenario-list">
  <div class="scenario-answer fragment fade-up">A → Binomial</div>
  <div class="scenario-answer fragment fade-up">B → Poisson</div>
  <div class="scenario-answer fragment fade-up">C → Hypergeometric</div>
  <div class="scenario-answer fragment fade-up">D → Geometric</div>
  <div class="scenario-answer fragment fade-up">E → Exponential</div>
  </div>
</div>

::: {.notes}
Let students answer before revealing the right side. The major skill is matching question to distribution, not formula recall.
:::

## The catch {.concept-slide}

<div class="eyebrow">Week 2 synthesis</div>

<div class="recursive-stack">
  <div class="recursive-line fragment fade-up">A distribution describes how probability is allocated.</div>
  <div class="recursive-line fragment fade-up">Its shape determines which observations are plausible.</div>
  <div class="recursive-line fragment fade-up">Different scientific mechanisms generate different distribution families.</div>
</div>

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
<div class="cliffhanger">
But in real science, the true distribution and its parameters are almost never known.
</div>
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-up}
<div class="final-question">
Next week: how can incomplete observations teach us about the process that generated them?
</div>
:::

::: {.notes}
End with the transition from probability to statistics. Probability assumes a model and asks what observations are likely. Statistics observes data and asks what model or parameter values are plausible.
:::

<script>
(function(){
function normPdf(x, mu = 0, s = 1) {
  return Math.exp(-0.5 * Math.pow((x - mu) / s, 2)) / (s * Math.sqrt(2 * Math.PI));
}

function drawNormalSvg(svg, mu, s) {
  if (!svg) return;

  const W = 700, H = 260, pad = 36;
  const xMin = -4, xMax = 4;
  const yMax = 1.05; // Fixed height so curve dynamically grows/flattens with sigma
  const baseline = H - pad;

  const mapX = (x) => pad + ((x - xMin) / (xMax - xMin)) * (W - 2 * pad);
  const mapY = (y) => baseline - (y / yMax) * (H - 2 * pad);

  // Generate main curve points
  const step = 0.02;
  let pdfPath = `M ${mapX(xMin).toFixed(1)} ${mapY(normPdf(xMin, mu, s)).toFixed(1)}`;
  for (let x = xMin + step; x <= xMax; x += step) {
    pdfPath += ` L ${mapX(x).toFixed(1)} ${mapY(normPdf(x, mu, s)).toFixed(1)}`;
  }

  // ------------------------------------------------------------
  // Correctly Grounded Polygon for μ ± 1σ
  // ------------------------------------------------------------
  const sigmaLower = Math.max(xMin, mu - s);
  const sigmaUpper = Math.min(xMax, mu + s);

  // 1. Start ON BASELINE at lower bound
  let sigmaPath = `M ${mapX(sigmaLower).toFixed(1)} ${baseline}`;
  // 2. Rise vertically to the curve
  sigmaPath += ` L ${mapX(sigmaLower).toFixed(1)} ${mapY(normPdf(sigmaLower, mu, s)).toFixed(1)}`;

  // 3. Follow the PDF curve up to upper bound
  for (let x = sigmaLower + step; x <= sigmaUpper; x += step) {
    sigmaPath += ` L ${mapX(x).toFixed(1)} ${mapY(normPdf(x, mu, s)).toFixed(1)}`;
  }
  sigmaPath += ` L ${mapX(sigmaUpper).toFixed(1)} ${mapY(normPdf(sigmaUpper, mu, s)).toFixed(1)}`;

  // 4. Drop vertically down to baseline
  sigmaPath += ` L ${mapX(sigmaUpper).toFixed(1)} ${baseline}`;
  // 5. Close path along baseline
  sigmaPath += ` Z`;

  // ------------------------------------------------------------
  // SVG Construction
  // ------------------------------------------------------------
  let html = '';

  // Faint ±1σ Shaded Area
  html += `<path d="${sigmaPath}" class="widget-sigma-area"/>`;

  // Full Normal PDF Curve
  html += `<path d="${pdfPath}" class="widget-path"/>`;

  // Baseline X-axis
  html += `<line x1="${pad}" y1="${baseline}" x2="${W - pad}" y2="${baseline}" class="widget-axis"/>`;

  // Dashed Center Line at μ
  const muX = mapX(mu);
  html += `<line x1="${muX}" y1="${pad}" x2="${muX}" y2="${baseline}" class="widget-line"/>`;

  // Dashed Boundary Lines at μ - 1σ and μ + 1σ
  const leftSigmaX = mapX(mu - s);
  const rightSigmaX = mapX(mu + s);

  if (leftSigmaX >= pad && leftSigmaX <= W - pad) {
    html += `<line x1="${leftSigmaX}" y1="${mapY(normPdf(mu - s, mu, s))}" x2="${leftSigmaX}" y2="${baseline}" class="widget-line-sigma"/>`;
  }
  if (rightSigmaX >= pad && rightSigmaX <= W - pad) {
    html += `<line x1="${rightSigmaX}" y1="${mapY(normPdf(mu + s, mu, s))}" x2="${rightSigmaX}" y2="${baseline}" class="widget-line-sigma"/>`;
  }

  // Label at μ
  html += `<text x="${muX}" y="${baseline + 20}" text-anchor="middle" class="widget-label active">μ = ${mu.toFixed(1)}</text>`;

  svg.innerHTML = html;
}

function initNormal() {
  const svg = document.getElementById('normalSvg');
  const mu = document.getElementById('normalMu');
  const sig = document.getElementById('normalSigma');
  const lab = document.getElementById('normalParams');

  if (!svg || !mu || !sig) return;

  function update() {
    const m = +mu.value;
    const s = +sig.value;
    drawNormalSvg(svg, m, s);
    if (lab) {
      lab.textContent = `𝒩(${m.toFixed(1)}, ${s.toFixed(2)}²)`;
    }
  }

  mu.addEventListener('input', update);
  sig.addEventListener('input', update);
  update();
}

function drawEmpiricalRuleSvg(svgId) {
  const svg = document.getElementById(svgId);
  if (!svg) return;

  const W = 700, H = 220, pad = 45;
  const mu = 0, s = 1;
  
  // 1. WIDEN X-RANGE: [-4.2, 4.2] zooms out horizontally
  const xMin = -4.2, xMax = 4.2;
  const baseline = H - pad; // y = 175

  const mapX = (x) => pad + ((x - xMin) / (xMax - xMin)) * (W - 2 * pad);
  
  // 2. INCREASE HEADROOM: yMax = 0.52 zooms out vertically
  const yMax = 0.52; 
  const mapY = (y) => baseline - (y / yMax) * (baseline - 25);

  function buildGroundedAreaPath(a, b, step = 0.02) {
    const startX = Math.max(xMin, a);
    const endX = Math.min(xMax, b);
    let path = `M ${mapX(startX).toFixed(1)} ${baseline}`;
    path += ` L ${mapX(startX).toFixed(1)} ${mapY(normPdf(startX, mu, s)).toFixed(1)}`;
    for (let x = startX + step; x <= endX; x += step) {
      path += ` L ${mapX(x).toFixed(1)} ${mapY(normPdf(x, mu, s)).toFixed(1)}`;
    }
    path += ` L ${mapX(endX).toFixed(1)} ${mapY(normPdf(endX, mu, s)).toFixed(1)}`;
    path += ` L ${mapX(endX).toFixed(1)} ${baseline} Z`;
    return path;
  }

  const step = 0.02;
  let pdfPath = `M ${mapX(xMin).toFixed(1)} ${mapY(normPdf(xMin, mu, s)).toFixed(1)}`;
  for (let x = xMin + step; x <= xMax; x += step) {
    pdfPath += ` L ${mapX(x).toFixed(1)} ${mapY(normPdf(x, mu, s)).toFixed(1)}`;
  }

  let html = '';

  // Empirical Rule Shaded Fills
  html += `<path d="${buildGroundedAreaPath(-3, 3)}" fill="rgba(123, 74, 181, 0.08)"/>`;
  html += `<path d="${buildGroundedAreaPath(-2, 2)}" fill="rgba(123, 74, 181, 0.14)"/>`;
  html += `<path d="${buildGroundedAreaPath(-1, 1)}" fill="rgba(123, 74, 181, 0.22)"/>`;

  // Normal PDF Curve
  html += `<path d="${pdfPath}" class="widget-path"/>`;

  // Baseline X-Axis
  html += `<line x1="${pad}" y1="${baseline}" x2="${W - pad}" y2="${baseline}" class="widget-axis"/>`;

  // Mean μ Line
  const muX = mapX(mu);
  html += `<line x1="${muX}" y1="${mapY(normPdf(0, mu, s))}" x2="${muX}" y2="${baseline}" class="widget-line"/>`;

  // Axis Labels
  const labels = [
    { x: -3, text: "−3σ" },
    { x: -2, text: "−2σ" },
    { x: -1, text: "−1σ" },
    { x:  0, text: "μ" },
    { x:  1, text: "+1σ" },
    { x:  2, text: "+2σ" },
    { x:  3, text: "+3σ" }
  ];

  labels.forEach(lbl => {
    html += `<text x="${mapX(lbl.x)}" y="${baseline + 20}" text-anchor="middle" class="widget-label">${lbl.text}</text>`;
  });

  svg.innerHTML = html;
}

});

function drawQuantileSvg(svgId) {
  const svg = document.getElementById(svgId);
  if (!svg) return;

  const W = 700;
  const H = 220;

  const leftPad = 38;
  const rightPad = 38;
  const topPad = 18;
  const bottomPad = 32;

  const mu = 0;
  const s = 1;

  const xMin = -4.2;
  const xMax = 4.2;

  const baseline = H - bottomPad;

  const mapX = (x) =>
    leftPad +
    ((x - xMin) / (xMax - xMin)) *
    (W - leftPad - rightPad);

  const yMax = 0.46;

  const mapY = (y) =>
    baseline -
    (y / yMax) *
    (baseline - topPad);

  // ------------------------------------------------------------
  // Build normal PDF
  // ------------------------------------------------------------

  const step = 0.02;

  let pdfPath =
    `M ${mapX(xMin).toFixed(1)} ` +
    `${mapY(normPdf(xMin, mu, s)).toFixed(1)}`;

  for (let x = xMin + step; x <= xMax; x += step) {
    pdfPath +=
      ` L ${mapX(x).toFixed(1)} ` +
      `${mapY(normPdf(x, mu, s)).toFixed(1)}`;
  }

  // ------------------------------------------------------------
  // Grounded probability-area helper
  // ------------------------------------------------------------

  function buildGroundedAreaPath(a, b) {
    const startX = Math.max(xMin, a);
    const endX = Math.min(xMax, b);
    let path =
      `M ${mapX(startX).toFixed(1)} ${baseline}`;
    path +=
      ` L ${mapX(startX).toFixed(1)} ` +
      `${mapY(normPdf(startX, mu, s)).toFixed(1)}`;
    for (let x = startX + step; x <= endX; x += step) {
      path +=
        ` L ${mapX(x).toFixed(1)} ` +
        `${mapY(normPdf(x, mu, s)).toFixed(1)}`;
    }
    path +=
      ` L ${mapX(endX).toFixed(1)} ` +
      `${mapY(normPdf(endX, mu, s)).toFixed(1)}`;
    path +=
      ` L ${mapX(endX).toFixed(1)} ${baseline} Z`;
    return path;
  }

  // ------------------------------------------------------------
  // Normal quantiles
  //
  // q05 ≈ -1.64485
  // q50 = 0
  // q95 ≈ +1.64485
  // ------------------------------------------------------------

  const q05 = -1.644854;
  const q50 = 0;
  const q95 = 1.644854;

  let html = "";

  // ------------------------------------------------------------
  // 5% accumulated probability
  // ------------------------------------------------------------

  html += `
    <path
      d="${buildGroundedAreaPath(xMin, q05)}"
      class="widget-area">
    </path>
  `;

  // ------------------------------------------------------------
  // Full normal density
  // ------------------------------------------------------------

  html += `
    <path
      d="${pdfPath}"
      class="widget-path">
    </path>
  `;

  // ------------------------------------------------------------
  // Baseline
  // ------------------------------------------------------------

  html += `
    <line
      x1="${leftPad}"
      y1="${baseline}"
      x2="${W - rightPad}"
      y2="${baseline}"
      class="widget-axis">
    </line>
  `;

  // ------------------------------------------------------------
  // Quantile lines
  // ------------------------------------------------------------

  const quantiles = [
    {
      x: q05,
      label: "5%",
      value: "q₀.₀₅"
    },
    {
      x: q50,
      label: "50%",
      value: "q₀.₅₀"
    },
    {
      x: q95,
      label: "95%",
      value: "q₀.₉₅"
    }
  ];

  quantiles.forEach(q => {
    const px = mapX(q.x);
    const py = mapY(normPdf(q.x, mu, s));
    html += `
      <line
        x1="${px}"
        y1="${py}"
        x2="${px}"
        y2="${baseline}"
        class="widget-line">
      </line>
    `;
    html += `
      <circle
        cx="${px}"
        cy="${py}"
        r="4"
        class="quantile-point">
      </circle>
    `;
    html += `
      <text
        x="${px}"
        y="${baseline + 17}"
        text-anchor="middle"
        class="widget-label">
        ${q.label}
      </text>
    `;
    html += `
      <text
        x="${px}"
        y="${baseline + 31}"
        text-anchor="middle"
        class="quantile-symbol">
        ${q.value}
      </text>
    `;
  });

  svg.innerHTML = html;
}

// Render on page load
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => {
  drawQuantileSvg("quantileSvg");
});

function cauchyPdf(x, x0 = 0, gamma = 1) {
  return 1 / (Math.PI * gamma * (1 + ((x - x0) / gamma) ** 2));
}

function drawTailCompareSvg(svgId) {
  const svg = document.getElementById(svgId);
  if (!svg) return;

  const W = 700;
  const H = 220;

  const leftPad = 38;
  const rightPad = 38;
  const topPad = 18;
  const bottomPad = 32;

  const baseline = H - bottomPad;

  const xMin = -4.2;
  const xMax = 4.2;

  const mapX = (x) =>
    leftPad +
    ((x - xMin) / (xMax - xMin)) *
    (W - leftPad - rightPad);

  // Use a shared y scale based on the larger peak
  const normalPeak = normPdf(0, 0, 1);         // ~0.399
  const cauchyPeak = cauchyPdf(0, 0, 1);       // ~0.318
  const yMax = Math.max(normalPeak, cauchyPeak) * 1.15;

  const mapY = (y) =>
    baseline -
    (y / yMax) *
    (baseline - topPad);

  function buildCurvePath(pdfFn, step = 0.02) {
    let path =
      `M ${mapX(xMin).toFixed(1)} ${mapY(pdfFn(xMin)).toFixed(1)}`;
    for (let x = xMin + step; x <= xMax; x += step) {
      path += ` L ${mapX(x).toFixed(1)} ${mapY(pdfFn(x)).toFixed(1)}`;
    }
    return path;
  }

  const normalPath = buildCurvePath(x => normPdf(x, 0, 1));
  const cauchyPath = buildCurvePath(x => cauchyPdf(x, 0, 1));

  let html = "";

  // axis
  html += `
    <line
      x1="${leftPad}"
      y1="${baseline}"
      x2="${W - rightPad}"
      y2="${baseline}"
      class="widget-axis">
    </line>
  `;

  // mean/center reference line
  html += `
    <line
      x1="${mapX(0)}"
      y1="${topPad}"
      x2="${mapX(0)}"
      y2="${baseline}"
      class="tail-center-line">
    </line>
  `;

  // normal
  html += `
    <path
      d="${normalPath}"
      class="widget-path">
    </path>
  `;

  // cauchy / heavy tail
  html += `
    <path
      d="${cauchyPath}"
      class="widget-path-blue">
    </path>
  `;

  // labels near curves
  html += `
    <text
      x="${mapX(2.15)}"
      y="${mapY(normPdf(2.15, 0, 1)) - 10}"
      class="tail-label tail-label-normal">
      normal
    </text>
  `;

  html += `
    <text
      x="${mapX(2.6)}"
      y="${mapY(cauchyPdf(2.6, 0, 1)) - 2}"
      class="tail-label tail-label-cauchy">
      Cauchy / heavy tail
    </text>
  `;

  // x-axis tick labels
  [-3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3].forEach(x => {
    html += `
      <text
        x="${mapX(x)}"
        y="${baseline + 18}"
        text-anchor="middle"
        class="widget-label">
        ${x === 0 ? "0" : x}
      </text>
    `;
  });

  svg.innerHTML = html;
}

// Render on page load
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => {
  drawTailCompareSvg("tailCompareSvg");
});

function drawMiniPmf(svgId, values, probs, yMax = 1) {
  const svg = document.getElementById(svgId);
  if (!svg) return;

  const W = 240;
  const H = 135;

  const left = 18;
  const right = 222;
  const top = 12;
  const baseline = 108;

  const mapY = p =>
    baseline - (p / yMax) * (baseline - top);

  const n = values.length;

  const mapIndex = i => {
    if (n === 1) return W / 2;
    return left + i / (n - 1) * (right - left);
  };

  let html = `
    <line
      x1="${left}"
      y1="${baseline}"
      x2="${right}"
      y2="${baseline}"
      class="mini-pmf-axis">
    </line>
  `;

  values.forEach((value, i) => {
    const x = mapIndex(i);
    const y = mapY(probs[i]);
    html += `
      <line
        x1="${x}"
        y1="${baseline}"
        x2="${x}"
        y2="${y}"
        class="mini-pmf-stem">
      </line>
      <circle
        cx="${x}"
        cy="${y}"
        r="4"
        class="mini-pmf-dot">
      </circle>
      <text
        x="${x}"
        y="${baseline + 15}"
        text-anchor="middle"
        class="mini-pmf-label">
        ${value}
      </text>
    `;
  });

  svg.innerHTML = html;
}

function drawDegenerate() {
  drawMiniPmf(
    "degeneratePmf",
    ["c"],
    [1]
  );
}

function drawDiscreteUniform() {
  const slider = document.getElementById("uniformK");
  const output = document.getElementById("uniformKValue");

  const k = Number(slider.value);

  output.textContent = k;

  const values =
    Array.from({ length: k }, (_, i) => i + 1);

  const probs =
    Array(k).fill(1 / k);

  drawMiniPmf(
    "uniformPmf",
    values,
    probs
  );
}

function drawBernoulli() {
  const slider = document.getElementById("bernoulliP");
  const output = document.getElementById("bernoulliPValue");

  const p = Number(slider.value);

  output.textContent = p.toFixed(2);

  drawMiniPmf(
    "bernoulliPmf",
    [0, 1],
    [1 - p, p]
  );
}

function choose(n, k) {
  if (k < 0 || k > n) return 0;

  let result = 1;

  for (let i = 1; i <= k; i++) {
    result *= (n - i + 1) / i;
  }

  return result;
}

function drawBinomial() {
  const nSlider = document.getElementById("binomialN");
  const pSlider = document.getElementById("binomialP");

  const nOutput = document.getElementById("binomialNValue");
  const pOutput = document.getElementById("binomialPValue");

  const n = Number(nSlider.value);
  const p = Number(pSlider.value);

  nOutput.textContent = n;
  pOutput.textContent = p.toFixed(2);

  const values =
    Array.from({ length: n + 1 }, (_, k) => k);

  const probs =
    values.map(k =>
      choose(n, k) *
      p ** k *
      (1 - p) ** (n - k)
    );

  drawMiniPmf(
    "binomialPmf",
    values,
    probs
  );
}

function drawGeometric() {
  const slider = document.getElementById("geometricP");
  const output = document.getElementById("geometricPValue");

  const p = Number(slider.value);

  output.textContent = p.toFixed(2);

  const values = Array.from({ length: 10 }, (_, i) => i + 1);

  const probs = values.map(t =>
    (1 - p) ** (t - 1) * p
  );

  drawMiniPmf(
    "geometricPmf",
    values,
    probs,
    Math.max(...probs) * 1.08
  );
}

function drawHypergeometric() {
  const nPopSlider = document.getElementById("hyperN");
  const kSuccessSlider = document.getElementById("hyperK");
  const sampleSlider = document.getElementById("hyperSample");

  const nOut = document.getElementById("hyperNValue");
  const kOut = document.getElementById("hyperKValue");
  const sampleOut = document.getElementById("hyperSampleValue");

  let N = Number(nPopSlider.value);
  let K = Number(kSuccessSlider.value);
  let n = Number(sampleSlider.value);

  // enforce valid parameter combinations
  K = Math.min(K, N);
  n = Math.min(n, N);

  kSuccessSlider.max = N;
  sampleSlider.max = N;

  kSuccessSlider.value = K;
  sampleSlider.value = n;

  nOut.textContent = N;
  kOut.textContent = K;
  sampleOut.textContent = n;

  const kMin = Math.max(0, n - (N - K));
  const kMax = Math.min(n, K);

  const values =
    Array.from(
      { length: kMax - kMin + 1 },
      (_, i) => kMin + i
    );

  const denom = choose(N, n);

  const probs = values.map(k =>
    choose(K, k) *
    choose(N - K, n - k) /
    denom
  );

  drawMiniPmf(
    "hypergeometricPmf",
    values,
    probs,
    Math.max(...probs) * 1.08
  );
}

function factorial(k) {
  let result = 1;

  for (let i = 2; i <= k; i++) {
    result *= i;
  }

  return result;
}

function drawPoisson() {
  const slider = document.getElementById("poissonLambda");
  const output = document.getElementById("poissonLambdaValue");

  const lambda = Number(slider.value);

  output.textContent = lambda.toFixed(1);

  // Enough support to show nearly all visible mass
  const kMax = Math.max(
    8,
    Math.ceil(lambda + 3 * Math.sqrt(lambda))
  );

  const values =
    Array.from({ length: kMax + 1 }, (_, k) => k);

  const probs = values.map(k =>
    Math.exp(-lambda) *
    lambda ** k /
    factorial(k)
  );

  drawMiniPmf(
    "poissonPmf",
    values,
    probs,
    Math.max(...probs) * 1.08
  );
}

drawDegenerate();
drawDiscreteUniform();
drawBernoulli();
drawBinomial();
drawGeometric();
drawHypergeometric();
drawPoisson();

function drawMiniDensity(svgId, pdf, xMin, xMax, options = {}) {
  const svg = document.getElementById(svgId);
  if (!svg) return;

  const W = 240;
  const H = 135;

  const left = 18;
  const right = 222;
  const top = 12;
  const baseline = 108;

  const steps = 180;

  const points = [];

  for (let i = 0; i <= steps; i++) {
    const x = xMin + (i / steps) * (xMax - xMin);
    const y = pdf(x);
    if (Number.isFinite(y)) {
      points.push([x, y]);
    }
  }

  const observedMax = Math.max(
    ...points.map(p => p[1]),
    0.001
  );

  const yMax = options.yMax || observedMax * 1.12;

  const mapX = x =>
    left +
    ((x - xMin) / (xMax - xMin)) *
    (right - left);

  const mapY = y =>
    baseline -
    (y / yMax) *
    (baseline - top);

  let curvePath = "";

  points.forEach(([x, y], i) => {
    curvePath +=
      `${i === 0 ? "M" : "L"} ` +
      `${mapX(x).toFixed(1)} ${mapY(y).toFixed(1)} `;
  });

  let areaPath =
    `M ${mapX(points[0][0]).toFixed(1)} ${baseline} `;

  points.forEach(([x, y]) => {
    areaPath +=
      `L ${mapX(x).toFixed(1)} ${mapY(y).toFixed(1)} `;
  });

  areaPath +=
    `L ${mapX(points[points.length - 1][0]).toFixed(1)} ${baseline} Z`;

  let html = `
    <path
      d="${areaPath}"
      class="mini-density-fill">
    </path>
    <path
      d="${curvePath}"
      class="mini-density-path">
    </path>
    <line
      x1="${left}"
      y1="${baseline}"
      x2="${right}"
      y2="${baseline}"
      class="mini-density-axis">
    </line>
  `;

  if (options.zeroLabel !== false) {
    html += `
      <text
        x="${mapX(0)}"
        y="${baseline + 15}"
        text-anchor="middle"
        class="mini-density-label">
        0
      </text>
    `;
  }

  svg.innerHTML = html;
}

function drawDirac() {
  const svg = document.getElementById("diracDensity");
  if (!svg) return;

  const baseline = 108;
  const center = 120;

  svg.innerHTML = `
    <line
      x1="18"
      y1="${baseline}"
      x2="222"
      y2="${baseline}"
      class="mini-density-axis">
    </line>
    <line
      x1="${center}"
      y1="${baseline}"
      x2="${center}"
      y2="25"
      class="dirac-stem">
    </line>
    <polygon
      points="${center - 6},31 ${center},18 ${center + 6},31"
      class="dirac-arrow">
    </polygon>
    <text
      x="${center}"
      y="${baseline + 15}"
      text-anchor="middle"
      class="mini-density-label">
      c
    </text>
    <text
      x="${center + 11}"
      y="30"
      class="dirac-area-label">
      area = 1
    </text>
  `;
}

function drawContinuousUniform() {
  const aSlider = document.getElementById("uniformA");
  const bSlider = document.getElementById("uniformB");

  const aOut = document.getElementById("uniformAValue");
  const bOut = document.getElementById("uniformBValue");

  let a = Number(aSlider.value);
  let b = Number(bSlider.value);

  // Keep a < b
  if (a >= b) {
    if (document.activeElement === aSlider) {
      a = b - 0.5;
      aSlider.value = a;
    } else {
      b = a + 0.5;
      bSlider.value = b;
    }
  }

  aOut.textContent = a.toFixed(1);
  bOut.textContent = b.toFixed(1);

  const height = 1 / (b - a);

  drawMiniDensity(
    "continuousUniformDensity",
    x => (x >= a && x <= b ? height : 0),
    -2.5,
    5.5,
    {
      yMax: Math.max(height * 1.2, 0.35)
    }
  );
}

function drawExponential() {
  const slider =
    document.getElementById("exponentialLambda");

  const output =
    document.getElementById("exponentialLambdaValue");

  const lambda = Number(slider.value);

  output.textContent = lambda.toFixed(2);

  drawMiniDensity(
    "exponentialDensity",
    t =>
      t >= 0
        ? lambda * Math.exp(-lambda * t)
        : 0,
    0,
    8
  );
}

function drawGamma() {
  const kSlider =
    document.getElementById("gammaK");

  const lambdaSlider =
    document.getElementById("gammaLambda");

  const kOut =
    document.getElementById("gammaKValue");

  const lambdaOut =
    document.getElementById("gammaLambdaValue");

  const k = Number(kSlider.value);
  const lambda = Number(lambdaSlider.value);

  kOut.textContent = k;
  lambdaOut.textContent = lambda.toFixed(2);

  const gammaPdf = t => {
    if (t < 0) return 0;
    return (
      lambda ** k *
      t ** (k - 1) *
      Math.exp(-lambda * t) /
      factorial(k - 1)
    );
  };

  // Wide enough to show the distribution as k changes.
  const xMax = Math.max(
    6,
    (k + 4 * Math.sqrt(k)) / lambda
  );

  drawMiniDensity(
    "gammaDensity",
    gammaPdf,
    0,
    xMax
  );
}

function drawGaussianDensity() {
  const muSlider =
    document.getElementById("gaussianMu");

  const sigmaSlider =
    document.getElementById("gaussianSigma");

  const muOut =
    document.getElementById("gaussianMuValue");

  const sigmaOut =
    document.getElementById("gaussianSigmaValue");

  const mu = Number(muSlider.value);
  const sigma = Number(sigmaSlider.value);

  muOut.textContent = mu.toFixed(1);
  sigmaOut.textContent = sigma.toFixed(1);

  drawMiniDensity(
    "gaussianDensity",
    x => normPdf(x, mu, sigma),
    -5,
    5,
    {
      zeroLabel: true
    }
  );
}

function lognormalPdf(x, muLog = 0, sigmaLog = 1) {
  if (x <= 0) return 0;

  return (
    Math.exp(
      -((Math.log(x) - muLog) ** 2) /
      (2 * sigmaLog ** 2)
    ) /
    (
      x *
      sigmaLog *
      Math.sqrt(2 * Math.PI)
    )
  );
}

function drawLognormalDensity() {
  const muSlider =
    document.getElementById("lognormalMu");

  const sigmaSlider =
    document.getElementById("lognormalSigma");

  const muOut =
    document.getElementById("lognormalMuValue");

  const sigmaOut =
    document.getElementById("lognormalSigmaValue");

  const muLog = Number(muSlider.value);
  const sigmaLog = Number(sigmaSlider.value);

  muOut.textContent = muLog.toFixed(2);
  sigmaOut.textContent = sigmaLog.toFixed(2);

  drawMiniDensity(
    "lognormalDensity",
    x => lognormalPdf(x, muLog, sigmaLog),
    0,
    12,
    {
      zeroLabel: true
    }
  );
}

function paretoPdf(x, xm = 1, alpha = 2) {
  if (x < xm) return 0;

  return (
    alpha *
    xm ** alpha /
    x ** (alpha + 1)
  );
}

function drawParetoDensity() {
  const slider =
    document.getElementById("paretoAlpha");

  const output =
    document.getElementById("paretoAlphaValue");

  const alpha = Number(slider.value);

  output.textContent = alpha.toFixed(2);

  drawMiniDensity(
    "paretoDensity",
    x => paretoPdf(x, 1, alpha),
    0,
    8,
    {
      zeroLabel: true
    }
  );
}

function drawCauchyDensity() {
  const x0Slider =
    document.getElementById("cauchyX0");

  const gammaSlider =
    document.getElementById("cauchyGamma");

  const x0Out =
    document.getElementById("cauchyX0Value");

  const gammaOut =
    document.getElementById("cauchyGammaValue");

  const x0 = Number(x0Slider.value);
  const gamma = Number(gammaSlider.value);

  x0Out.textContent = x0.toFixed(1);
  gammaOut.textContent = gamma.toFixed(1);

  drawMiniDensity(
    "cauchyDensity",
    x => cauchyPdf(x, x0, gamma),
    -8,
    8,
    {
      zeroLabel: true
    }
  );
}

function choose(n,k){ if(k<0||k>n) return 0; k=Math.min(k,n-k); let r=1; for(let i=1;i<=k;i++) r=r*(n-k+i)/i; return r; }
function binomPmf(n,p,k){ return choose(n,k)*(p**k)*((1-p)**(n-k)); }
function initBinom(){
const svg=document.getElementById('binomSvg'), nEl=document.getElementById('binomN'), pEl=document.getElementById('binomP'), mode=document.getElementById('binomMode'), kEl=document.getElementById('binomK'), probEl=document.getElementById('binomProb'), model=document.getElementById('binomModel');
if(!svg||!nEl||!pEl||!mode||!kEl) return;
function update(){
const n=+nEl.value,p=+pEl.value; kEl.max=n; let k=Math.min(+kEl.value,n); kEl.value=k;
const vals=Array.from({length:n+1},(_,i)=>binomPmf(n,p,i)); const max=Math.max(...vals);
let prob=0; vals.forEach((v,i)=>{ if((mode.value==='eq'&&i===k)||(mode.value==='le'&&i<=k)||(mode.value==='ge'&&i>=k)) prob+=v; });
const W=700,H=260,pad=36,barW=(W-2*pad)/(n+1)*.78, gap=(W-2*pad)/(n+1)*.22;
let html=`<line x1="${pad}" y1="${H-pad}" x2="${W-pad}" y2="${H-pad}" class="widget-axis"/>`;
vals.forEach((v,i)=>{ const active=(mode.value==='eq'&&i===k)||(mode.value==='le'&&i<=k)||(mode.value==='ge'&&i>=k); const x=pad+i*(barW+gap+((W-2*pad)-(n+1)*(barW+gap))/(n+1)); const h=v/max*(H-2*pad); html+=`<rect x="${x}" y="${H-pad-h}" width="${barW}" height="${h}" fill="${active?'rgba(123,74,181,.75)':'rgba(152,162,179,.35)'}" rx="4"/>`; });
html+=`<text x="350" y="28" text-anchor="middle" class="widget-label">highlighted bars = selected probability question</text>`;
svg.innerHTML=html; probEl.textContent=prob.toFixed(3); model.textContent=`Binomial(${n}, ${p.toFixed(2)})`;
}
[nEl,pEl,mode,kEl].forEach(el=>el.addEventListener('input',update)); update();
}
document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded',function(){ initNormal(); drawEmpiricalRuleSvg(); initBinom(); });
if(window.Reveal){ Reveal.on('ready',function(){ initNormal(); drawEmpiricalRuleSvg(); initBinom(); }); }
})();
</script>
